reason: E1 and E2 directly support Hf coating forming dense HfO2 and reducing mass gain on VZrHfNbTa, with E2 specifying a 120 μm coating. E3 supports the baseline oxidation behavior and 200 h test condition for a similar RHEA, but the cited alloy is different and forms CrTaO4, not explicitly VZrHfNbTa. The 50% reduction is an overstatement not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Hf coating forms a dense, protective HfO2 layer during oxidation
HfO2 layer reduces oxygen ingress and oxidation mass gain

VZrHfNbTa alloy baseline oxidation forms less protective CrTaO4-based or mixed scales
